item.title: Cancelling pedestrian crossing, 20th November
item.description:
When the pedestrian crossing is pressed then the request automatically cancel out before the green man appears, even if people are standing at the crossing. This happens almost every time I am at the crossing, so I have to repeat pressing the button. Please remove the automatic cancellation. People who don't know the fault assume they are broken and end up crossing without the green man creating a very dangerous situation. The automatic cancellation adds nothing to this crossing except danger.

item.title: Unauthorised objects in the public highway preventing parking, 20th November
item.description:
I am writing to raise a formal complaint regarding the ongoing use of traffic cones and other unauthorised objects being placed in the road outside properties 1, 2 and 3 Alstone Lane, Cheltenham (Struck Hill area). The occupants of these properties, who I understand are council tenants, are repeatedly placing cones and other objects in the road to prevent other members of the public from lawfully parking in these spaces. This originally started with the occupants of number 3, but has now spread to the neighbouring properties, with multiple residents taking it upon themselves to restrict access to public parking spaces. The situation is becoming increasingly frustrating. Parking in this area is already extremely difficult, and it is unacceptable that certain individuals believe they have the right to reserve public parking spaces for their own use. What makes matters worse is the attitude of the occupants when people move the cones to park lawfully. Residents are being met with rudeness and confrontation simply for wanting to use available parking spaces. I appreciate that parking can be challenging for everyone, but public roads and unrestricted parking spaces cannot be claimed or reserved by individual residents through the use of cones or other obstructions. I would therefore ask the council to investigate this ongoing issue, clarify the rules to the occupants involved and take appropriate action to prevent this behaviour from continuing. This is happening on a daily basis and needs addressing before the situation escalates further.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 2, Alstone Lane, Kingsditch, Cheltenham, Cheltenham
Report on FixMyStreet
